## Summary {-}

::: {.box}
**Answer.** Open the second terminal in 2028, not 2027. The wait costs about 4 million euros of lost volume but avoids a 12 million euro capacity gap that opens if demand falls short.

1. Delay the commitment by one year.
2. Sign a flexible lease option now.
:::

## Situation {#sec-situation}

Harbourline handles 1.2 million containers a year. Demand grew 6% a year over the last five years [@porter1985]. This section sets out what is known and what is not.

A paragraph that ends with a colon introduces a list:

1. Capacity at the first terminal is 1.4 million containers.
2. Demand reaches that limit in about three years.

## Options {#sec-options}

@sec-situation shows the limit. @tbl-options compares the options.

| Option | Cost (EUR m) | Risk |
|--------|-------------:|------|
| Build now | 120 | High |
| Build in 2028 | 105 | Medium |
| Lease first | 40 | Low |

: Options compared {#tbl-options}

*Source: team estimates from the case exhibits.*

## Recommendation

Choose the lease. It keeps the choice open and limits the downside [@porter1985, p. 12].
